scenario: Bounded local coordination leases over explicit historical write-job membership

stages.label: explicit-ledgers-retain-historical-membership
stages.explanation: Two independent private ledgers capture the same explicit three-position catalog. Exact create replay and show preserve each identity; bounded pages start unclaimed and retain cursor arithmetic.

stages.label: ordinary-workers-compete-within-one-ledger
stages.explanation: Three ordinary CLI processes are launched before responses are collected. Two compete for position 1: exactly one succeeds and one receives busy. Position 2 succeeds independently; process overlap, throughput and maximum capacity are not measured.

stages.label: generation-cas-and-historical-replies
stages.explanation: Releasing position 1 permits a fresh lease ID and generation 2. A stale generation cannot release it; exact old claim/release replies remain historical. A genuinely discarded position-3 claim reply is recovered without extending its expiry, then released.

stages.label: independent-ledgers-and-source-free-coordination
stages.explanation: A second ledger can claim the same catalog position while the first ledger's generation 2 remains active: exclusivity is scoped to one ledger. With both catalogs and six job/target directories absent, ledger show/page/replay and a new claim/release still work. Every path returns in finally.

stages.label: invalid-requests-and-stale-cas-refuse
stages.explanation: Malformed bounds, identities and cursors refuse. Reusing operation IDs with changed parameters, stale release identities, already released new operations and an active claim refuse without advancing captured jobs or changing accepted history.

stages.label: released-heads-preserve-jobs-and-authority-boundaries
stages.explanation: All five previously claimed ledger positions end released; the secondary ledger's third position remains unclaimed. Twelve unique immutable operations, completed write jobs, historical catalogs, blocked restore jobs and source/live Store observations remain distinct. No lease API advances a job or grants domain authority.

limits: A claim coordinates one explicit catalog position within one ledger. A second ledger can simultaneously claim that same position; no cross-ledger or external fencing exists.
The captured write jobs are already completed. Leases do not inspect job phases, establish pending work, execute steps, authenticate workers or grant domain write authority.

Three ordinary CLI children are launched before responses are collected. The result demonstrates one accepted current claimant per position in this ledger; overlap, throughput and maximum capacity are not measured.
Release compares the latest lease ID, generation and self-declared worker. A new claim after release increments generation and creates a new lease ID; stale release cannot replace it.
Exact operation replay returns an immutable historical receipt, including its original expiry, even after release or reclaim. It does not establish current ownership or extend time.
One actual validated claim reply is discarded and recovered by exact replay. Its ephemeral comparison digest is not exported.

Show, page, exact create replay, new claim and release use only the private ledger after capture. Eight captured catalog/job/target paths are temporarily unavailable and every path returns in finally; blocked restore jobs never move.

Pages observe one ledger transaction and do not read job states. Metadata comparisons exclude directory times changed by rename; public Store comparisons exclude only top-level governance observed_at.

Duration, expiry, clock-regression, resource limits and SQLite durability depend on the specified local protocol. This ordinary scenario does not wait for expiry, regress clocks, exhaust the operation cap, inject storage errors or prove power-loss behavior.

No new fault worker, forced interruption, partial control write, arbitrary code execution or external LLM is introduced. Self-declared agreement and safe scheduling do not establish semantic truth or independent expertise.
